summary: In a fiction excerpt from Book 3, the narrator reviews country-specific adoption agencies (Cradle of Hope for Russian orphans, Children and Families, Inc. for Ecuadorian children, International Adoption Assistance, Inc. for Brazilian orphans) and finds them slow, asking about a fast track for a healthy newborn. She travels with Lou to Quetzal Manor, a former Carmelite convent on the Hudson, partly for his company after a threatening call to Paula and an encounter with a Hispanic thug outside Paula's building. The imposing, Gothic-looking manor unsettles her as she arrives, and Lou offers to accompany her inside.
one_line: A narrator visits the imposing former Carmelite convent Quetzal Manor on the Hudson to meet someone who already knows more about her than she knows about them.
key_facts: The narrator found that country-specific adoption organizations for emerging-world babies still worked the same way and were slow.
Cradle of Hope specialized in orphaned Russian children.
Children and Families, Inc., provided adoptions for Equadorian children.
International Adoption Assistance, Inc., handled Brazilian orphans.
The narrator asked whether there was a new fast track for a brand-new healthy baby in just a few months, and the question was always taken as a joke.
The narrator drove to Quetzal Manor in her old Toyota with Lou along, after convincing him to come.
The narrator wanted Lou with her for security after a threatening phone call to Paula and a Hispanic thug who accosted the narrator outside Paula's apartment building.
The drive went up Riverside Drive, then the Henry Hudson Parkway, and the Hudson was described as an ardent highway into the heart of America.
Lou had less of a hangover than usual that morning, still elevated by Sarah's momentary brush with consciousness.
Carly had told the narrator that Quetzal Manor was once a Carmelite convent dating from the middle of the last century.
Quetzal Manor featured endless arches of cut stone, turrets and gargoyles, and was described as a monument to Church authority.
The narrator compared the manor's appearance to a Gothic movie set and a brooding homage to medieval torture.
The narrator's cold still lingered, so her mind did not feel fully working as they parked under a huge oak tree in front.
Lou asked, 'Want me to go in with you?'
